title: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx for a line through the origin

sections.skill: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx for a line through the origin

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx for a line through the origin
questions.prompt: A line passes through the origin and (4, 6). For any other point (x, y) on the line (x ≠ 0), the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (x, 0), (x, y) is similar to the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (4, 6). Use this to write the equation of the line.
questions.prompt_markup:
A line passes through the origin and (4, 6). For any other point (x, y) on the line (x ≠ 0), the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (x, 0), (x, y) is similar to the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0), (4, 6).
Use this to write the equation of the line.
questions.correct_answer: y = 1.5x (because y ÷ x = 6 ÷ 4 for x ≠ 0, and the origin also fits)

questions.skill: Use similar triangles to derive y = mx for a line through the origin
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A line passes through the origin with slope m. Use a slope triangle from (0, 0) to a point (x, y) on the line (x ≠ 0) to explain why every point on the line satisfies y = mx.
questions.prompt_markup: A line passes through the origin with slope m. Use a slope triangle from (0, 0) to a point (x, y) on the line (x ≠ 0) to explain why every point on the line satisfies y = mx.
questions.required_method: The slope triangle with vertices (0, 0), (x, 0), (x, y) is similar to the triangle with run 1 and rise m, so y ÷ x = m ÷ 1 and y = mx. The point (0, 0) also satisfies y = m · 0. Any equivalent explanation is accepted.

questions.domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
questions.skill: Use rotated slope triangles to explain the slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: A slope triangle for line p has a run of 3 and a rise of 2. Rotating it 90° counterclockwise gives a slope triangle for a line q perpendicular to p. What are the run and rise of the rotated triangle, and what is the slope of q?
questions.prompt_markup:
A slope triangle for line p has a run of 3 and a rise of 2. Rotating it 90° counterclockwise gives a slope triangle for a line q perpendicular to p.
What are the run and rise of the rotated triangle, and what is the slope of q?
questions.correct_answer: Run -2 and rise 3 (or run 2 and rise -3); the slope of q is -3/2.

questions.domain: Geometry: Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations
questions.skill: Use rotated slope triangles to explain the slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines
questions.standard_level: High school (Common Core high-school standard; this bank places it at Grade 10 as a second forward step. This is an instructional choice, not an official grade assignment.)
questions.prompt: Use slope triangles to explain why two parallel, non-vertical lines have equal slopes.
questions.prompt_markup: Use slope triangles to explain why two parallel, non-vertical lines have equal slopes.
questions.correct_answer: A transversal makes equal corresponding angles with the two lines, so their slope triangles have the same angles and are similar; similar triangles have equal rise ÷ run.
